voice.name: Okay Cool Narrator (designed)
voice.design: VoxCPM2 voice design from a text description only (a woman in her mid thirties; warm, natural, mid-pitched American voice; expressive, unhurried; design seed 15), saved as a Voice Studio profile. No real person's audio.

intro.text: Hi! Welcome in. I'll be your guide for this little tour. Quick confession: I'm an AI voice, made on Mike's Mac Studio, down in his basement. Mike spent thirteen years on a carrier network, taking the hard tickets and making the changes that had to go right. Scroll at your own pace. I'll keep up.
intro.mood: warm, bright and playful, welcoming a guest

tldr.text: Okay, the short version, for the busy ones. Thirteen years at Charter. Circuits, escalations, and overnight maintenance on production routers, from BGP policy to quality of service. Then the dev-ops team, on a platform that found and secured hundreds of thousands of devices. Next? A small team, anywhere from Madison to Milwaukee.

contact.text: Want to talk? His email is right here, and he really does reply quickly. Okay, cool. Now, on to what he's built.

projects.text: First up, GrowYear: a garden planner he took from an idea to a finished app, live on the internet. Then the work itself: the tools he built at Charter, and the projects he runs at home.
projects.mood: bright and curious, showing it off a little

story.text: So here's how he got here. Tech school. Then Charter, in 2013, turning up fiber circuits for business customers. A spreadsheet tool the whole team ended up using. A new set of standards after a big merger. Then Python, overnight maintenance windows, and a spot on the dev-ops team.
story.mood: warm and fond, telling a story

before.text: Now, where it all started. Years before any of the rest, Mike was wiring up garage doors, plant waterers, and pepper sensors, all by hand. Tinkerers are a stubborn bunch.

lab.text: And now, the workshop beneath the house. Watch your head. A control room where nothing important happens without his okay. A stock dashboard that pinned people's tweets right onto the price chart. A house voice named Thaddeus, who reads tornado warnings at three in the morning. Monitoring that makes failures loud. And a garden planner called GrowYear, which is live on the internet now. His family uses most of it. Some of them even like it.
lab.mood: proud and playful, giving a tour

garden.text: A gardener who starts young gets about sixty gardens in a lifetime. Sixty. That's not very many, is it? That's why Mike builds these tools: so the computers take more of the chores, and his family gets more of him.

built.text: Okay, this part is fun. The pictures, the music, and, yes, me: all made on Mike's Mac Studio. And the page itself comes to you from a Raspberry Pi in his basement, by way of a satellite. That's the tour! Thanks for stopping by.
built.mood: excited and full of wonder, then a cheerful goodbye

pemberton.text: Good evening, and welcome back to Okay Cool Radio. I am Lord Pemberton, and I am obliged by contract to introduce the following number. It was composed entirely by machine, in a basement in Milton, Wisconsin, about a tiny website and its little robots. I am told it is cute. I remain unconvinced. Here it is. Okay, Cool.
